correct.description: A try-with-resources statement does not require a catch or finally block[cite: 122]. A traditional try statement requires at least one of the two[cite: 123].

After opening both resources in the try-with-resources statement, T is printed[cite: 124]. Then the try-with-resource completes and closes the resources in reverse order from which they were opened[cite: 125]. After W is printed, an exception is thrown; however, the remaining resource is still closed and D is printed[cite: 126]. The exception thrown is then caught and E is printed[cite: 127]. Last, the finally block is run, printing F. Therefore the answer is TWDEF[cite: 128].

A try-with-resources statement uses parentheses rather than brackets for the try section[cite: 129]. This is likely subtler than a question that you’ll get on the exam, but it is still important to be on alert for details[cite: 130].
